blocks.text: Release overview
This repository’s iOS 10.0 record maps to the September 13, 2016 public appearance that Apple identifies as iOS 10.0.1; Apple’s consumer history presents the launch notes under “iOS 10 - iOS 10.0.1.”

The launch substantially expanded Messages, opened Siri and Maps to supported app integrations, added on-device Photos organization and Memories, introduced the Home app, and redesigned several core system experiences.

blocks.text: Release overview
iOS 10.1 reached the public release channel on October 24, 2016.

The update introduced a beta Portrait Camera mode for iPhone 7 Plus, added detailed transit support in Japan, refined Messages effects, addressed a range of reliability problems, and shipped a documented security update.
Release overview
iOS 10.2 reached the public release channel on December 12, 2016.

The update introduced Apple’s TV app in the United States, added and redesigned emoji, improved Photos and Messages, expanded HomeKit notifications and accessibility support, and delivered a broad security update.
Release overview
iOS 10.2.1 reached the public release channel on January 23, 2017.

The patch improved peak-workload power management to reduce unexpected iPhone shutdowns and addressed documented security issues across push notifications, call history, contacts, the kernel, archives, device unlocking, WebKit, and Wi-Fi.
Release overview
iOS 10.3 reached the public release channel on March 27, 2017.

The update added Find My AirPods, expanded Siri and CarPlay integrations, reorganized Apple ID settings, enabled cross-device iTunes movie rentals, extended several built-in apps, exposed in-app rating APIs to developers, and shipped a substantial security update.

blocks.text: Release overview
iOS 10.3.1 reached the public release channel on April 3, 2017.

Apple characterized the patch as a bug-fix and security update; its advisory specifically documents a Wi-Fi vulnerability that could allow arbitrary code execution on the wireless chip from within range.
Release overview
iOS 10.3.2 reached the public release channel on May 15, 2017.

Apple described the release as a bug-fix and security update, while its advisory details corrections across audio, contacts, graphics, iBooks, the kernel, notifications, Safari, telephony, and WebKit.
Release overview
iOS 10.3.3 reached the public release channel on July 19, 2017.
Apple described the release as a bug-fix and security update; its advisory documents corrections across contacts, the kernel, Messages, notifications, Safari, telephony, WebKit, and the Wi-Fi chip.

events.summary: This repository’s iOS 10.0 record maps to the September 13, 2016 public appearance that Apple identifies as iOS 10.0.1; Apple’s consumer history presents the launch notes under “iOS 10 - iOS 10.0.1.” The launch substantially expanded Messages, opened Siri and Maps to supported app integrations, added on-device Photos organization and Memories, introduced the Home app, and redesigned several core system experiences. This article retains the repository’s existing 10.0 route identity, does not create a separate 10.0.1 record, and does not infer beta-specific timing or an undocumented build document.

blocks.text: Public release

The local 10.0 Public milestone is dated September 13, 2016 and explicitly notes iOS 10.0.1. Apple’s security advisory gives that same day for iOS 10.0.1, while its consumer page groups the launch material as iOS 10 through iOS 10.0.1.
What changed

The launch substantially expanded Messages, opened Siri and Maps to supported app integrations, added on-device Photos organization and Memories, introduced the Home app, and redesigned several core system experiences.

changes.title: Expressive Messages and iMessage apps
changes.canonicalSummary: Messages added bubble and full-screen effects, Tapback, handwriting, Digital Touch, rich links, an iMessage app storefront, and stickers.
changes.summary: The launch broadened conversation effects and introduced an app-extension ecosystem inside Messages.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched first-party Apple documentation to the audited public-release version and date.

citations.locator: More Personal and Expressive Ways to Message

changes.title: Siri app integrations
changes.canonicalSummary: Supported messaging, calling, photo, ride, payment, fitness, and automaker apps could expose selected actions through Siri.
changes.summary: Apple opened defined Siri tasks to participating third-party apps through the iOS 10 extension model.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched first-party Apple documentation to the audited public-release version and date.

changes.title: Maps redesign and extensions
changes.canonicalSummary: Maps gained a new interface, proactive destinations, along-route search, parked-car context, and extensions for reservations and ride booking.
changes.summary: The release reworked navigation and let supported services complete reservations or rides from Maps.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched first-party Apple documentation to the audited public-release version and date.

changes.title: Photos recognition and Memories
changes.canonicalSummary: Photos added local face, object, and scene recognition, map-based organization, and automatically assembled Memories and movies.
changes.summary: The new organization and search tools analyzed the local library and surfaced themed collections.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched first-party Apple documentation to the audited public-release version and date.

changes.title: Home app for HomeKit
changes.canonicalSummary: The new Home app provided one place to manage HomeKit accessories, scenes, notifications, shared access, and supported automation.
changes.summary: iOS 10 added a first-party interface for controlling compatible home accessories and scenes.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched first-party Apple documentation to the audited public-release version and date.

citations.locator: Home App for Smarter Home Automation

changes.title: Core app and system experience redesigns
changes.canonicalSummary: Apple Music and News received redesigned interfaces, while Raise to Wake, richer notifications, widgets, and a reorganized Control Center changed common interactions.
changes.summary: The major release refreshed media and news navigation alongside the Lock Screen, notification, widget, and Control Center experience.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched first-party Apple documentation to the audited public-release version and date.

changes.title: iOS 10 launch security fixes
changes.canonicalSummary: The launch addressed documented vulnerabilities across system validation, networking, media parsing, privacy boundaries, the kernel, and WebKit; iOS 10.0.1 added a kernel-memory disclosure fix and inherited that baseline.
changes.summary: Apple’s two linked advisories document the security content associated with the September 13 public software.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched Apple’s dated security advisory to the audited public-release version and date.

blocks.text: Public release
Apple’s dated records place the public iOS 10.1 appearance on October 24, 2016. This article covers that public release and does not infer beta-specific timing or an undocumented build number.
What changed

The update introduced a beta Portrait Camera mode for iPhone 7 Plus, added detailed transit support in Japan, refined Messages effects, addressed a range of reliability problems, and shipped a documented security update.

changes.title: Portrait Camera beta on iPhone 7 Plus
changes.canonicalSummary: A beta Portrait Camera mode used depth information to keep the subject sharp while softening the background on iPhone 7 Plus.
changes.summary: The update introduced Apple’s first documented public beta of the depth-effect portrait mode for iPhone 7 Plus.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched first-party Apple documentation to the audited public-release version and date.

changes.title: Japan transit directions
changes.canonicalSummary: Maps added major rail, subway, ferry, national-bus, and local-bus coverage for Tokyo, Osaka, and Nagoya, including station layouts and fare comparisons.
changes.summary: The release expanded transit navigation in Japan with network, station, and fare detail.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched first-party Apple documentation to the audited public-release version and date.

changes.title: Messages effects controls
changes.canonicalSummary: Messages added effect replay and allowed effects to play when Reduce Motion was enabled, alongside several conversation-display and media fixes.
changes.summary: The update made expressive effects easier to replay and more compatible with the Reduce Motion setting.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched first-party Apple documentation to the audited public-release version and date.

changes.title: Camera, connectivity, and system reliability
changes.canonicalSummary: The release corrected documented Camera, Photos, Bluetooth, AirPlay, Mail, Safari, widget, alarm, backup, and other reliability problems.
changes.summary: Apple’s notes identify a broad maintenance pass across imaging, wireless accessories, built-in apps, and system behaviors.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched first-party Apple documentation to the audited public-release version and date.

citations.locator: iOS 10.1 — Camera and Photos; Other improvements and fixes

changes.title: iOS 10.1 security fixes
changes.canonicalSummary: The update addressed CVE-tracked issues across code-signing validation, networking, contacts, media parsing, backups, the kernel, archives, and WebKit.
changes.summary: Apple’s advisory documents multiple security corrections included with the October 24 public release.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched Apple’s dated security advisory to the audited public-release version and date.

What changed

The update introduced Apple’s TV app in the United States, added and redesigned emoji, improved Photos and Messages, expanded HomeKit notifications and accessibility support, and delivered a broad security update.

changes.title: TV app in the United States
changes.canonicalSummary: The new U.S.-only TV app unified discovery, resumption, recommendations, compatible video apps, and access to iTunes purchases and rentals.
changes.summary: iOS 10.2 delivered Apple’s consolidated television-discovery interface for supported U.S. users and services.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched first-party Apple documentation to the audited public-release version and date.

changes.title: Expanded and redesigned emoji
changes.canonicalSummary: More than one hundred emoji were added and existing artwork was redrawn with additional visual detail.
changes.summary: The release expanded the emoji set across people, food, animals, sports, professions, and other groups.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched first-party Apple documentation to the audited public-release version and date.

changes.title: Photos and Messages improvements
changes.canonicalSummary: Live Photos stabilization and frame rate improved, People grouping became more accurate, RAW camera support expanded, and Messages gained two additional full-screen effects.
changes.summary: The update refined photo capture and organization while adding love and celebration effects to Messages.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched first-party Apple documentation to the audited public-release version and date.

changes.title: HomeKit, accessibility, and reliability improvements
changes.canonicalSummary: HomeKit notifications expanded, VoiceOver and switch-control issues were corrected, and Apple documented Bluetooth, FaceTime, voicemail, Mail, and Safari fixes.
changes.summary: The maintenance portion of iOS 10.2 improved accessory notifications, assistive technologies, connectivity, communications, and built-in apps.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched first-party Apple documentation to the audited public-release version and date.

changes.title: Find My AirPods
changes.canonicalSummary: Find My iPhone could display an AirPods location and play a sound on one or both earbuds to help locate them.
changes.summary: The update brought supported AirPods into Apple’s device-location workflow.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched first-party Apple documentation to the audited public-release version and date.

changes.title: Expanded Siri app capabilities
changes.canonicalSummary: Siri gained supported workflows for bill payment and status, ride scheduling, and selected vehicle status and controls in participating apps.
changes.summary: Apple broadened the tasks that payment, ride-booking, and automaker apps could expose through Siri.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched first-party Apple documentation to the audited public-release version and date.

changes.title: CarPlay shortcuts and music controls
changes.canonicalSummary: CarPlay added status-bar shortcuts to recently used apps and expanded access to Up Next, albums, playlists, and music categories.
changes.summary: The release reduced navigation friction between CarPlay apps and broadened Apple Music access in the vehicle interface.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched first-party Apple documentation to the audited public-release version and date.

changes.title: Account, media, and built-in app improvements
changes.canonicalSummary: Settings gained a unified Apple ID view; iTunes movie rentals became available across devices; Maps, Calendar, Home, Podcasts, and accessibility behaviors also expanded or improved.
changes.summary: iOS 10.3 combined account-management and cross-device media changes with documented additions across several built-in apps.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched first-party Apple documentation to the audited public-release version and date.

changes.title: In-app App Store ratings API
changes.canonicalSummary: New App Store APIs let apps request a rating or review without sending the user out of the app.
changes.summary: Apple documented the iOS 10.3 interface for requesting App Store feedback within an app.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched first-party Apple Developer documentation to the audited public release and consumer notes.
